title: Range-Based for Loops
learningObjectives: Choose value, reference and const-reference loop variables.
Read and modify collection elements appropriately.
Recognize when a manual index is genuinely needed.
Use range-based loops for safer direct traversal.

understand.concept: Range-based for visits each element in a range without requiring a manual index. Use const auto& for read-only access and auto& for in-place changes.
understand.whyItMatters: It reduces index mistakes and makes element-oriented intent clear.
understand.explain: Choose value, const reference, or mutable reference depending on whether copying or modification is needed.

examples.title: Read array
examples.explanation: Visits each element; scalar copies are inexpensive.

examples.title: Sum vector
examples.code: std::vector<int> v{5,10,15}; int sum=0;\nfor(int item:v) sum+=item;
examples.explanation: A direct element loop is sufficient when index is not needed.

examples.title: Transform array
examples.explanation: Mutable references let each element change.

practise.guidedTask: For Range-Based for Loops, trace each example in a table showing the loop's initial state, condition result, body action, update step, and final state. Identify the termination point and boundary behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a small C++ exercise focused on Range-Based for Loops. Include at least three test cases (typical, boundary and termination/invalid-input case where relevant), trace the loop iterations, and explain why it stops or skips/continues as intended.
hints: Write down the loop's starting state.
Trace the condition before/after each pass according to loop type.
Check that every continuing path progresses toward termination.
Test boundary values and early-exit paths.
Count passes explicitly to catch off-by-one errors.

questions.explanation: const reference binds without copying and cannot mutate.
